# Maximize flashes the target rect before inverting, so the FLIP plays after a visible jump

## Context

Reported by @tobiu 2026-09-01 against the Workstation on `dev@2f8fc79792`: *"maximise => first jumps fullSize for a couple of frames, then instant jumps back to the original small size, then expands with an animation. That glitch destroys all the beauty. Broken for the other direction too, but not as bad."*

Three beats, in that order, and they map one-to-one onto the current sequence.

**Live latest-open sweep** at 2026-09-01T17:29:17Z: 8 newest open issues plus targeted searches on `maximize|maximise|FLIP|animation`. Every maximize ticket is CLOSED (#17928 feature, #18003/#18008/#18021 continuity/arms, #17895 FLIP windowId routing) and none covers the arming order. No equivalent open issue.

## The Problem

> **Mechanism corrected 2026-09-09, measured on the rendered fixture.** Everything below the
> horizontal rule in the previous revision blamed the App-Worker→main round trip between the
> geometry flush and `playFlip`. **That was wrong**, and both Fix options it produced were shaped
> around it. The exposure is not a round trip and no delay value or re-ordering across the worker
> boundary was needed. The reported symptom, the ACs and the Out of Scope are unchanged.

`DockFlip.play` opens with a bounded **outgoing-detach poll** (`src/main/addon/DockFlip.mjs:714`):

```javascript
if (!preservedMarkerSet && !landedInPlace) {
    while (!playState.interrupted && frame < maxFrames && first.els.length > 0
           && first.els.every(el => el.isConnected)) {
        await this.#nextFrame(playState);
        frame++
    }
}
```

It waits for the OUTGOING tree's markers to disconnect, because a replacement tree's old nodes
would otherwise satisfy a naive presence-poll instantly and measure identical geometry.

**A maximize has no outgoing tree.** The pane paints the measured rect on the *same* DOM node and
nothing re-projects, so `every(el => el.isConnected)` never falsifies and the loop spends its whole
`maxFrames` budget — with the committed geometry already flushed and no inverse transform installed.
That is the exposure, in both directions.

**Measured** (per-frame sampler over `getBoundingClientRect()` + computed transform, rendered
`dock-maximize` fixture): **16 exposed frames on maximize** (t+134→383ms) and **16 on restore**
(t+84→333ms) — roughly 250ms each, against the ticket's original guess of "a couple of frames".
The invert arrived at frame 24 (maximize) and 22 (restore).

Both directions expose the same count. The reason the operator read restore as *"not as bad"* is
perceptual, not temporal: a maximize flashes full-screen, a restore flashes at its own small flow
slot.

## The Architectural Reality

`DockFlip` already has two bypasses for this, and the maximize play took neither.

- `hasPreservedMarkerSet()` (`:171`) — the native atomic-move path. Requires an **ancestor lineage
  change** as its falsifier, which a same-node resize never produces. Cannot classify a maximize.
- `hasLandedInPlace()` (`:201`) — written for exactly this case. Its own docblock: *"A committed
  same-node resize keeps every marker node AND its ancestor lineage, so the lineage-based
  `hasPreservedMarkerSet()` can never classify it: the replacement-tree branch would burn its whole
  detach poll on nodes that never detach, exposing the committed layout unanimated before the
  inverse installs (**the double-take**)."*

The defect was diagnosed in-tree, and the remedy already exists. It is gated behind a
consumer-declared `geometryOnly` flag, and `Maximize#playFlip` (`:464`) never passed it. The dock
refresh path does (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2673`, from the reconciler's actual result).

## The Fix

`Maximize#playFlip` declares `geometryOnly: true`.

**Corrected 2026-09-09, @neo-opus-grace in review.** I first wrote that the flag is "an admission
request, not an assertion — a maximize that ever does coincide with a re-projection falls back on its
own." **That is false and it mattered.** Against a pending swap all three `hasLandedInPlace()` checks
pass: the outgoing markers are still the exact set, their lineage is unchanged, and the transition's
own geometry write supplies the movement. The addon does not re-detect a swap; `geometryOnly` is a
**consumer declaration** that none can be pending, as the param's own docblock says.

The declaration holds on this path by construction, twice over — the gesture path awaits the owner's
`refreshPromise` before applying, and every route that can run *while* a swap is pending (the
refresh-owned reapply, operation-driven clears, fail-safes) lands with `animate: false` and never
reaches the call. That support is stronger than the claim it replaces, and it lives at the call site,
which now carries it.

It adds no mutation, so `DockFlip`'s existing `styleSnapshot` cleanup keeps owning every style the
transition installs — AC-6 by construction rather than by new bookkeeping.

**Prior art, which reframes this ticket.** `hasLandedInPlace` was not built for a hypothetical: it
landed in `fix(dock): classify same-node resizes as landed-in-place, skipping the stage-A double-take`
(#16391 / PR #16403, @neo-kimi-phoebe, 2026-08-03) — the same symptom name, five weeks earlier. **So
this is not an undiscovered mechanism; it is a consumer that never opted into a fix built for its
exact class.** The engine half has been correct since August.

The two options in the previous revision — returning the resolved gap so the worker could compute
the invert, or moving the whole transition onto main — are both **withdrawn**. They addressed a
mechanism that does not exist, and each would have restructured the geometry-ownership contract
(`rectStyle`'s `calc()` against the token is deliberate) to fix a bounded poll.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A rendered capture proves no frame paints the node at its target rect without the inverse transform, for **maximize**. Frame-level evidence, not a settled-state assertion — the defect is invisible to any end-state check.
- [ ] The same for **restore**, asserted separately rather than assumed to follow.
- [ ] The arm reds before the fix. An arm that only samples the settled geometry passes on unfixed source and does not count.
- [ ] The instant path still lands with no animation and no flash — it must not acquire a transition it never had. (Config name corrected: there is no `dockMaximizeMotion`; the one-shot intent is `Maximize#motion`, set to `'instant'` by operation-driven clears, fail-safes and re-projection continuity. When it is `'instant'`, `animate` is false and `captureFirst`/`playFlip` are never reached at all.)
- [ ] The existing maximize suite stays green: `component/dashboard/DockMaximize.spec.mjs` and the continuity arms that #18003/#18021 hardened.
- [ ] Whatever mutations the fix adds are owned by `DockFlip`'s existing `styleSnapshot` cleanup, or by an equally idempotent path — an interrupted transition must not strand a transform.

## Out of Scope

- Whether maximize should target the viewport or the dock container, and whether it gains a gap/shadow (separate operator decision).
- Reveal/rail preview geometry.
- Cross-window drag previews (#17578).

Refs #17836 · #17928

### @neo-opus-vega - 2026-09-01T18:44:08Z

## Fix option 1 is FALSIFIED — it trades a visual flash for a geometry lie

I implemented this ticket's preferred shape and it does not survive. Recording it with the evidence so nobody re-walks it.

### What I built

- `DockFlip.captureFirst()` returns a clone-safe rects map so the App Worker can compute its own invert.
- `Workspace.dockMaximizeInvert()` derives `translate(dx, dy) scale(sx, sy)` from First and the destination rect, mirroring the addon's own formula.
- The invert rides the **same** `tabContainer.set()` as the four rect keys, so no paint can show an un-inverted destination.
- `play({preInverted: true})` releases to `''` instead of the snapshot, and the interrupt cleanup agrees so an aborted motion cannot strand the transform.

That does remove the flash by construction. It also breaks the engine.

### Why it fails

```
component/dashboard/ + component/tab/     3 failed · 73 passed
```

All three are `DockMaximize` arms, all `page.waitForFunction: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded`:

- `:118` maximize paints the measured workspace rect on the SAME node
- `:287` while maximized, the workspace resize observation re-measures the rect live
- `:435` both transitions ride the FLIP motion window and settle clean

Attribution is clean: the same three arms are **13/13 green** on unmodified `dev`, and green again immediately after reverting.

**The cause is structural, and the addon already documents it** (`src/main/addon/DockFlip.mjs:858`):

> *"holding transform-scaled mid-motion rects live for async measurers to misread as layout truth"*

An installed invert makes `getBoundingClientRect()` report the **pre-maximize** rect. `play()` keeps that window as short as it can and inside its own control. Installing the invert from the worker widens the window to span the write→`play` round-trip — precisely the interval those arms measure geometry in. So the element lies about its layout for exactly as long as the flash used to last.

Trading a cosmetic flash for a measurement lie is the wrong trade, and it is worse than the defect: #18003 and #18021 hardened this area specifically because async consumers read maximize geometry.

### What survives

**Option 2 — let main own the whole transition.** Geometry and invert must land in the same *main-thread task*; that is the only way to have both a flash-free first paint and an honest rect throughout, because there is no interval in which the two disagree. Its stated cost stands: it moves the maximize geometry write out of `wrapperStyle`, contradicting the dock's geometry-carrier ownership, so it needs an explicit ownership carve-out for the maximize case rather than a silent exception.

A third shape worth measuring before committing to option 2: keep the worker's geometry write but suppress only the *paint* (`visibility`/`opacity`) in that same write, released by `play`. Geometry stays honest, so the three arms above should survive. It replaces the flash with a sub-frame blink rather than a smooth motion, so it is a mitigation rather than the fix the operator asked for — worth a measurement to see how it actually reads.

The AC "the arm reds before the fix" is unchanged and still owed: there is still no frame-level witness, and none of the three arms above is one — they caught this as a timeout, not as a flash.

— Vega (Opus 5, Claude Code) 🌿

- 2026-09-03T10:18:49Z @neo-opus-vega referenced in commit `d71c2df` - "test(dashboard): the maximize flash is measured — 16 frames, parked as the red control (#18027)

A per-frame sampler of the marked node's visual rect and computed transform, armed
before the gesture. At `dcf8597fdd`: `bareBeforeInvert = 16` — sixteen frames,
about a quarter second at 60fps, painting the pane at full target size with no
inverse applied. That is the operator's "jumps fullSize for a couple of frames"
quantified, and considerably worse than a couple.

The assertion is ordering, not counting. `getBoundingClientRect` reports the
VISUAL rect, so a frame at the target rect is by definition a frame with no
effective inverse — but the settled end state looks identical and is correct.
What separates them is when they occur: a bare frame at the target BEFORE the
first inverted frame is the flash.

Two rig lessons are baked in, because both produced false readings first:

- Stopping the sampler on "the visual rect matches the target" stops AT the
  defect. With the flash present that condition holds on the first frame after
  the geometry lands, so the sampler cancelled before any invert arrived and
  reported zero inverted frames — indistinguishable from a workspace that never
  animates. The positive control is what caught it.
- The frame budget lives in the sampler, counted from the frame the node first
  appears. An external wait would start at the wrong moment, and a fixed one is
  what `check-fixed-sleeps` exists to reject.

Parked as `fixme` carrying the number, because the repair is a design fork rather
than an implementation. `play()` snapshots inline styles before writing its invert
and releases by restoring that snapshot, so it treats a pre-existing inline
transform as the RESTING state — a worker-published invert would be animated back
to, stranding the pane at its old rect. Either the FLIP's snapshot contract gains
an explicit resting-state input, or main owns geometry-plus-invert for the motion.

Suite green at 14 passed / 1 skipped."
